title: Ghanaian Meat Pie
author: Monae Findley
desc: Four cups of flour to a cup and a third of cold salted butter, chilled thirty minutes, rolled a quarter inch and cut into six-inch rounds.
longDesc: The Ghanaian bakery pie, sold warm in paper bags at every bus station. Four cups of all-purpose flour, a cup and a third of cold salted butter and half a cup of vegetable shortening are pulsed to small chunks with a quarter teaspoon of baking powder, then six tablespoons of ice cold water until the dough clumps, and chilled thirty minutes. The filling is ground chicken or turkey with onion, carrot and scallion, cooked in stages — onions five minutes, carrot ten on low, then the scallions and meat for ten. The dough divides into eight, rolls to a quarter inch, and is cut into six-inch rounds. It bakes at 350 for forty-five minutes until golden.
ingredients: 1 1/3 cups salted butter, in its cold state
2 tbsp garlic-and-coconut chilli sauce — the source names a branded product
// The pastry step also calls for black pepper, which is not in the printed ingredient list. See the note.
steps: Add the carrot and cook 10 minutes on low.
Add the scallions and the meat and cook 10 minutes.
Season the filling with the chilli sauce, garlic powder, onion powder, ginger powder, salt and pepper, and let it cool.
For the pastry: pulse the flour, the cold butter and the shortening with the baking powder to small chunks.
Add the ice cold water until the dough clumps.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees Fahrenheit.
Divide the dough into 8, roll to 1/4 inch and cut 6-inch rounds.
Fill each round, fold, seal the edges and brush with egg wash.
Bake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes, until golden.
chefTips: Butter in its cold state, and ice cold water. That is the whole of pastry and the source is right to specify it twice.
Small chunks, not breadcrumbs. Visible pieces of butter are what make it flaky rather than short.
Thirty minutes chilling is a minimum. An hour is better and the dough rolls without fighting you.
Cool the filling completely before it goes near the pastry. Warm filling melts the butter and you lose the layers.
A quarter inch and six-inch rounds gives eight large pies. Ghanaian bakery pies are substantial, not canapés.
Forty-five minutes at 350 is a long bake for a small pie, and it is what gets the thick pastry cooked through. Judge by golden.
Note the source names a branded garlic-and-coconut chilli sauce. Any garlicky chilli sauce works, or lean on the three powders.
commonMistakes: Filling the pastry while the meat is still warm.
Rolling thinner than a quarter inch, which splits.
Pulling them at twenty-five minutes, when the pastry is still raw inside.
sources: Adapted from 'Ghanaian Meat Pie', mycleo.tv. BYLINE AS PRINTED: 'Written by Monae Findley'. Date as printed: 'Published on August 31, 2022'. Ingredients TWO-PASS.

A YIELD CONFLICT, both readings recorded: one pass printed '8 meat pies' and another printed 'Not specified'. The method does say to divide the dough into 8, which corroborates the first reading, and eight is used above on that basis.

Ingredients exactly as printed: '4 cups of all purpose flour'; '1 +1/3 cups of salted butter in its cold state'; '1/2 cup of vegetable shortening'; '1/4 teaspoon baking powder'; '6 Tablespoons of ice cold water'; 'Egg wash'; '2 scallions, thinly sliced'; '1/2 medium onion, small dice'; '1 medium carrot, cubed'; '1 pound ground chicken or turkey'; '2 tablespoons EssieSpice Coco-For -Garlic Sauce'; '1/2 garlic powder' — one pass gave '1/2 tsp'; '1/2 teaspoon onion powde' (sic, truncated as printed); '1/2 teaspoon ginger powder'; salt and pepper to taste.

A BRANDED INGREDIENT, flagged: the source specifies 'EssieSpice Coco-For -Garlic Sauce', a proprietary product. It is described above generically as a garlic-and-coconut chilli sauce so the recipe is usable without it, and the branded name is recorded here rather than in the ingredient line.

METHOD SOURCING CAVEAT, stated plainly: THE METHOD IS SINGLE-PASS AND UNVERIFIED. The second fetch returned only the fact that there are 'seven numbered steps' without their content, so the filling stages, the pastry technique, the chill time, the roll-out dimensions and the bake are all from one pass. The quantities are TWO-PASS; the method is not.

Method as reported on that single pass: onions 5 minutes; add carrot and cook 10 minutes on low; add scallions and meat and cook 10 minutes. Crust: pulse flour, cold butter and shortening to small chunks, add water until the dough clumps, chill 30 minutes, preheat to 350°F. Divide into 8, roll to ¼ inch, cut 6-inch rounds. Bake '350°F for 45 minutes until golden'.

A MISPRINT OR OMISSION IN THE SOURCE, flagged and not corrected: the crust step reads 'sift the flour add your baking powder, black pepper and baking powder' — BAKING POWDER IS NAMED TWICE and BLACK PEPPER IS NOT IN THE INGREDIENT LIST. 'onion powde' is also truncated as printed. None of these is silently fixed; the black pepper is noted in the ingredient list as an unlisted call.
NO TIPS appear on the page. The chef tips above are this collection's own, drawn from the technique the recipe specifies rather than from source text.

A SECOND SOURCE EXAMINED AND ITS LIMITS: 'The Tastiest Corned Beef Pie (Turnover)', fafagilbert.com, 13 February 2021, BYLINE AS PRINTED 'by Fafa Gilbert'. Its ingredient list is TWO-PASS and it is useful for the dish's identity — 'Make this easy to follow Corned Beef Turnover recipe which is popularly referred to as Meat Pie in Ghana.' Pastry: '300g of Self Raising Flour', '25g of flour for dusting', '150g of Cold Grated Butter', '1 teaspoon of Salt', '1 Egg Yolk', '1 teaspoon of Caraway seeds (optional)', '1 tablespoonful of Milk Powder or 60ml of Whole or Evaporated Milk'. Filling: a tin of prime corned beef, '100g of slow cooked Baby Plum/Cherry or Sun-dried Tomatoes', '3 large sliced Banana Shallots or 2 large Onions', half a teaspoon each of red chilli flakes and coarse ground aniseed or fennel, a tablespoon each of olive oil and butter, '2 tablespoonful of Greek Yogurt', half a teaspoon of milled black peppercorns, and salt to taste, noting corned beef is generally salty. IT IS NOT PUBLISHED because ITS METHOD IS VIDEO ONLY — no written method, no temperature and no times appear on the page — and the author describes it as 'Ghanaian inspired'. Its grated-cold-butter technique is worth knowing and is recorded here.

SOURCES REJECTED, recorded: a 'Flaky Ghanaian Meat Pie' on foodienotachef.com puts its recipe card behind a scroll-to-unlock gate, showing only a date (19 February 2026), no byline and no quantities; The African Gourmet's air-fryer version, bylined 'Ivy, The African Gourmet', gives no measures at all, calling for 'Cooked ground beef or chicken' and puff pastry; and a Food Network result was for NIGERIAN meat pies, a different cuisine.

NO GHANAIAN BAKERY-STYLE PASTRY RECIPE with full quantities AND a complete written method was found. This is the best available and its method's single-pass status is disclosed. A reader should treat it as the weakest-sourced entry in the Ghanaian baked goods.
storage: 3 days refrigerated, 3 months frozen baked or unbaked.
reheating: A 350-degree oven for 10 to 15 minutes. Never the microwave, which makes the pastry limp.
healthBenefits: Ground chicken or turkey is leaner than the beef most meat pies use.
Ginger and garlic carry documented anti-inflammatory compounds.
High in protein and genuinely filling.
culturalNote: The meat pie came to West Africa with the British and was kept because it travels — sold warm from glass cases at lorry parks, eaten one-handed on a tro-tro. The Ghanaian version runs smaller on spice and larger on pastry than the Nigerian, and the corned-beef turnover is its own well-loved branch.
